title: Comparing Values
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know the comparison operators that give back True or False.
idea: A comparison asks a yes or no question about two values, and the answer is always True or False. == means equal, != means not equal, < is less than, > is greater than, <= is less than or equal, and >= is greater than or equal. Also remember that a single = assigns a value while == compares two values, and mixing them up is a very common mistake.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change score = 80 to score = 40 and press Run. The line for score > 50 should turn into False.

practice.text: Set age = 11. Print whether age is greater than or equal to 10.
practice.hint: Put a comparison inside print(). The operator >= means greater than or equal to, and the answer will be True or False.
practice.starterTip: Try print(age >= 10) on the second line. With age 11, you should see True.

practice.text: Compare the strings "blue" and "Blue" with == and print the result.
practice.hint: Use == inside print() to ask whether the two are equal. Python cares about capital letters in strings.
practice.starterTip: Try print("blue" == "Blue"). Lowercase b and uppercase B are different, so expect False.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if output is False showing case-sensitive string compare.

quiz.question: What does == mean?

options.text: Check if two values are equal

quiz.correct: Right, == checks if two values are equal.
quiz.wrong: A single = assigns. A double == asks whether they are equal.

quiz.question: What does print(5 > 3) show?
quiz.correct: Yes, 5 is greater than 3, so it prints True.
quiz.wrong: Comparisons print True or False, not the numbers.

quiz.question: What is 10 != 10?
quiz.correct: Right, they are equal, so "not equal" is False.
quiz.wrong: != means not equal. 10 is equal to 10, so the answer is False.
